messages:
ashley (sre-oncall): Pager: multiple NCCL communicator timeouts observed on gpu-pool-05 during model-v2.3 canary (tensor-parallel=4). Impacting inference for a subset of tenants, intermittent 500s and hanging requests. Paging oncall.

pagerduty-bot: [ALERT] pg: oncall@sre - incident triggered: NCCL_COMM_TIMEOUT on gpu-pool-05 (auto-escalation). Priority: P1 -> Paging.

ashley (sre-oncall): Quick summary: started seeing elevated latencies ~08:22 UTC, by 08:25 we had several stuck workers with NCCL errors. Canary was rolled to ~10% traffic. Early hypothesis: multi-GPU collective failing during kv-cache warmup / long sequence lengths.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Can you paste the container logs + nvidia-smi from the affected node? Also what changed recently (driver/kernel/docker runtime)?

ashley (sre-oncall): Pasting excerpts from container logs (truncated):
```
[2026-03-15 08:25:17] ERROR: NCCL WARN Call to ncclAllReduce returned NCCL_UNRECOVERABLE, rank 0
[2026-03-15 08:25:17] ERROR: nccl_comm.c: timeout waiting for async progress
[2026-03-15 08:25:18] ERROR: CUDA kernel failed: cudaErrorIllegalAddress
[2026-03-15 08:25:19] WARN: tensor-parallel: rpc stall detected, pids: 1123,1124,1125,1126
```

ashley (sre-oncall): And `docker logs` shows repeated communicator reconnect attempts and eventual exit of worker processes.

maria (eng-ml): Could be communicator mismatch after the runtime patch we pushed yesterday (kernel/perf). Two quick mitigations: 1) route traffic off the canary to the last-good model (v2.2), 2) disable high-performance interconnect for the affected node (NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1) while we gather logs. Also enable NCCL_DEBUG=INFO for deeper traces.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Agreed. If we can fallback to single-GPU variant for the canary or route to dedicated pool that uses the older runtime, do that now. Also run these commands on the node: `sudo dmesg | tail -n 200`, `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.free,memory.total,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 1`, and `kubectl logs -n runtime svc/worker-1123 -c runner`.

ashley (sre-oncall): Executing now. dmesg shows NIC reset messages around 08:24: `mlx5_core 0000:5e:00.0: CARD_EVENT_RESET`, and repeated `NVRM: RmWatchdog: GPU at PCI:0000:5e:00: GPU has fallen off the bus`. nvidia-smi snapshot:
```
GPU 0: 64% util, 1024MiB free / 24576MiB total
GPU 1: 0% util, 512MiB free / 24576MiB total
GPU 2: 96% util, 128MiB free / 24576MiB total
GPU 3: Unresponsive (No data) -> cudaErrorNoDevice or driver reset
```

ashley (sre-oncall): So we have a NIC/PCIe level flapping on that node which is killing a GPU device mid-inference. That explains NCCL timeouts.

elaine (support): Customer impact: Acme-Inc reported increased 500s starting 08:23 UTC. Their dashboards show 6-8% of requests failing or timing out. Support has DMs open with them.

customer-ops: Confirmed, we started getting 500s at 08:23. Our retries mask some errors but production traffic saw latency spikes. Please keep us posted.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Immediate plan: 1) Roll traffic off canary to v2.2 (rollback). 2) Drain gpu-pool-05 node, cordon and remove from rotation. 3) Restart affected worker pods after cordon. 4) Collect full NCCL debug logs and NIC driver logs for postmortem. I can push a temporary routing rule to move canary traffic back.

ashley (sre-oncall): Initiating rollback of model-v2.3 -> v2.2 for canary traffic now. infra-bot, trigger rollback.

infra-bot: Rollback initiated: model-service/canary -> model-v2.2. Rolling traffic to previous variant (10% -> 0%).

ashley (sre-oncall): Also cordoning node gpu-pool-05 and starting a drain. Will set label `maintenance:comm-failure`.

infra-bot: Node cordon/drain started: gpu-pool-05. Pods are evicting.

maria (eng-ml): Long-term: add a pre-deploy multi-GPU collective stress test to the canary pipeline (random sequence lengths, kv-cache warmup) and verify system-level flakiness (PCIe/NIC resets) handling. Also consider pinning driver versions for dedicated pools.

sanjay (eng-runtime): For immediate debug, please capture `nccl-tests` reproducer if possible and run with `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL` and `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0` (force sockets), and try `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` to rule out IB as a cause. Also capture driver stack traces: `sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/0000:5e:00/information` and `sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 500`.

ashley (sre-oncall): Support notified customer and applied traffic rollback. Initial metrics post-rollback show errors dropping to baseline within ~90s.

elaine (support): Sending templated update to Acme-Inc: "We've rolled back to last known stable model and are investigating a GPU/PCIe host-level failure that impacted a small set of requests. We'll follow up with a postmortem and timeline."

customer-ops: Thanks. We'll monitor; please share when you have more details.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Collected additional logs - kernel shows repeated `mlx5_core` resets and `GPU has fallen off the bus` correlated with the NCCL failures. Attaching small excerpt for the record:
```
Mar 15 08:24:22 gpu-pool-05 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:5e:00.0: CARD_EVENT_RESET
Mar 15 08:24:22 gpu-pool-05 kernel: NVRM: RmWatchdog: GPU at PCI:0000:5e:00: GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 15 08:24:23 gpu-pool-05 systemd[1]: container-runner.service: main process exited, code=exited status=132
```

ashley (sre-oncall): Handoff note: I'm handing off to night oncall in 25m (sanjay will take follow-up). Current status: rollback complete, affected node drained, customer notified, incident declared mitigated but under investigation. Will open postmortem ticket and attach logs.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Taking follow-up. I'll spin up a repro job on a separate isolated pool to attempt to reproduce with nccl-tests and reproduce FLR. If reproducible, we'll mark as infrastructure vs runtime.

maria (eng-ml): Also adding a model-safety gate: block canaries that increase TP beyond 2x concurrency for 24h on pools without validated driver/firmware.

ashley (sre-oncall): Incident: Mitigated -> rollback + node drain. Opening SEV2 postmortem. Will include timeline, root cause (NIC/PCIe causing GPU detach -> NCCL timeouts), customer impact, and follow-ups (driver pin, pre-deploy stress tests, improved canary rollback automation).

infra-bot: Incident severity updated -> SEV2 (mitigated). Postmortem ticket created: PM-2026-0315-23.

elaine (support): Closing customer update with ETA for postmortem: 48 hours.

customer-ops: Appreciated. Keep us CC'd on the postmortem.

ashley (sre-oncall): Last note: if anyone finds anything new in the logs after drain, drop it here. Otherwise I'll handoff in 25m and mark follow-ups assigned to sanjay/maria.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Acknowledged. I'll take ownership of the postmortem and follow-ups.

(End of thread)
